discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, starting with the observation of the superfluid-Mott insulator quantum phase transition

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universitat Munich

subfield: Condensed matter and atomic physics: quantum many-body physics and quantum simulation
motivation: In 1998 Jaksch, Zoller and coworkers showed that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner, Bloch and colleagues used this proposal to observe the superfluid-Mott insulator transition. It was the first clean, controlled realization of a quantum phase transition in an interacting many-body system. This work turned Feynman's idea of quantum simulation into a working experimental science. Zoller's theory programme defined the field. Bloch and Greiner then developed quantum gas microscopes, which image correlated matter atom by atom. They used them to observe antiferromagnetic order, string patterns and entanglement growth in Hubbard systems, and to measure entanglement entropy directly. These platforms now test ideas that condensed matter theory could only calculate before: quantum criticality, fractionalization, many-body localization and strange-metal transport. Their impact is foundational and lasting, and it connects atomic physics, condensed matter and quantum information.
